name: General Matter
summary: General Matter is building domestic uranium-enrichment capacity for low-enriched uranium and HALEU. It raised a $50 million Founders Fund-led Series A in April 2025, with no public valuation disclosed.
overview: General Matter is developing uranium-enrichment capacity in the United States, focused on the low-enriched uranium and high-assay low-enriched uranium needed by the existing and next generation of reactors. The company is tackling a strategic supply-chain gap rather than building a reactor itself.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: General Matter raised $50 million in a Founders Fund-led Series A; its valuation was not disclosed.

bull_case: A durable domestic fuel shortage and government support for advanced reactors create a significant strategic market if General Matter can licence and operate enrichment capacity. Its announced $900 million HALEU supply contract signals meaningful customer and policy relevance.
bear_case: Uranium enrichment is a regulated, capital-intensive industrial business with long permitting and construction cycles. Contract announcements do not eliminate licensing, financing, technical or geopolitical risk.

intelligence.description: A nuclear-fuel company pursuing domestic uranium-enrichment capacity for LEU and HALEU.

metrics.label: Latest valuation
metrics.note: Valuation was not announced with the Series A

company: General Matter is working to build U.S. uranium-enrichment capacity, with a focus on low-enriched uranium and HALEU for advanced reactors. It is part of a broader effort to rebuild domestic nuclear-fuel supply chains that have long depended on foreign enrichment capacity.

The company raised a $50 million Founders Fund-led Series A in April 2025; its valuation was not disclosed. In January 2026, General Matter announced a $900 million contract to produce and supply HALEU, a material commercial milestone but not equity financing.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Fuel availability is a binding constraint on the next wave of advanced nuclear projects. General Matter is therefore exposed both to a large strategic opportunity and to the regulatory and execution hurdles inherent in an enrichment business.

changed.text: Announced a $900M contract to produce and supply HALEU for advanced reactors.

takeaways: The confirmed equity event is a $50M Series A; the valuation was not disclosed.
The $900M HALEU contract is commercial demand, not a funding round.
Licensing, construction and reliable production are the decisive underwriting milestones.
